utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not sure you've answered my question, and I'm going to ask it again. Please clarify why you put the word "asanacija" in brackets after the phrase "burying of the bodies."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Because that's what I was talking about, it was an interpretation of burying of the bodies, that's why I put it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Again, my understanding goes back to the phrase out of the JNA lexicon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So you chose to ignore the official CLSS translation and imposed your own, as it were, understanding of the word; is that --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean, somewhere along this line, in a footnote I have the CLSS definition of what the phrase means as a footnoted thing. I'm not ignoring it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let's come to the third one. "Finally, he made it clear that his unit could no longer deal with these issues, and that if 'no one' takes responsibility, he would be forced to 'let the prisoners go.'". Is that phrase in the irregular combat report of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, sir, and I think I said it a little bit before, that I did recognise it in looking at it. That is a technical inaccuracy on my part, and again I invite the Court to go back to the document and not rely on this as a direct quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why did you put that in quotation marks? Did you genuinely believe that's what Vinko Pandurevic had written in the irregular combat report of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: I'd love to be able to tell you the exact reason why I did it in 2000, but I just don't have the ability to say that. I mean, the reality is it is a wrong quote and it shouldn't be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you check this document before you signed it off?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So you saw those errors, did you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Obviously not, because in this particular context if I saw them, I wouldn't let them go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I thought you agreed with me that there is scarcely a more important document in this whole case. You didn't see that you'd misquoted it twice and imposed upon it your own interpretation of a word in a language you don't understand?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, sir, and I hope that when one goes back and looks at the Krstic transcripts, that in fact the actual issue of what the document said and what it meant would have been explored there. I don't think that this was something that was left askew at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's not my point, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Okay, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You wrote it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and I've acknowledged that it is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you knew what it was going to be used for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I -- I acknowledged that it was inaccurate, it's not the literal translation, and again, you know, I believe that it has been dealt with prior. But if not, certainly, I mean, my position is that we should go back to the original document and not to rely on a quote from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you knew, presumably, that it was going to be published?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: In so much as published by ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, made a public document in the Krstic trial, which had by then started.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: It was going to be tendered as an exhibit, yes, sir. I guess "published" is -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to give you the opportunity to assess yourself and your work. Just imagine for a minute that you did not write that and you were reviewing it as, for example, a Defence expert. How would you assess those few sentences as an example of expert document analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Again, sir, I take it as a technical inaccuracy. I acknowledge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Score it 1 out of 10, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can stop here on this. You keep qualifying it as a technical error. Why is it technical and not a substantive one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I -- and I'm sure Defence counsel will go into this more, but I don't believe that it changes the context of the discussion that was underway and what this means, and I'm sure we'll explore that down the line. So, I mean, it's a technical inaccuracy on my part that I misconstrued the actual translation of the document. I do not believe that it changes the overall context of the discussion, and again I think we're going to hear more about that down the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go to the point, please, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The phrase you used earlier when you were answering questions to Mr. Ostojic was that you thought your objectivity was such that you always strove to be fair and technically accurate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Yes correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is that passage of your report, interpreting the interim combat report of the 15th of July, technically accurate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: No, sir. I believe that we've acknowledged that it is not. Certainly I acknowledge that it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Left as it stands, is it fair?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed].
utterances.text: Again, it's inaccurate, but I don't believe that, when I look at this as from the original document, that it changes my opinion as to what it means. So whether it's fair or not is not something I -- I'm qualified to comment on. It certainly will be an issue for the Trial Chamber to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is it professional?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he's made his point very clear, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move to -- let's move to whatever you have in mind, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't want to move to anything else this morning, so if that's a convenient time to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can stop here, adjourn. Mr. Butler, thank you so much. We'll continue tomorrow morning. Mr. McCloskey, working on the assumption that tomorrow, hopefully, Mr. Haynes will conclude his cross-examination, as things stand at the moment, do you have a re-examination or are you planning for one, in which case could you give us an indication of the expected duration?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and I hope one session will do it. There's a -- I am going to go look at the documents that I think have been -- are now relevant, and I'll try to get them cut down and then get a better estimate. And, of course, I'll revise it depending on how far we go with this cross, but I should have a better estimate for tomorrow. As you know, I hope I can do this in an hour and a half. I really want this to be over with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st of January, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
